newsitem.title: UK: Baltic Index again marks weaker Ldn freight rates.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Index again marks weaker Ldn freight rates.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) opened the week with a fresh decline, by 10 points to 1,020, on an easier market in most key routes.
Shipbrokers noted that the Capesize Tubarao/Rotterdam sub-index was off slightly while US Gulf/Japan continued to head down.
They said that the sector again looks like being characterised this week by weak nearby grains fixtures.
"A large supply of tonnage remains readily available in the US Gulf, overhanging the market," one said.
Fixtures cited on Monday included Vitastar 54,000 tonnes heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for 20-25 September at $18.50 without combination to Dreyfus.
It was reported on Friday that Dreyfus also took Oceanic Enterprise 56,700 minmax heavy grains US Gulf/Japan for 20-26 September at $19.00, again without combination.
Ore fixtures are reported to include Atlantic Leader 70,000 tonnes Tuburao/Cigading end-September/beginning October at $10.50/$10.80 to Cetragpa.
Among timecharters 1996-built Cherokee 162,000 dwt del China obtained $10,000 daily Septtember trip via Richards Bay redelivery Spain from HMM.
Biffex futures were again lower across the board in reaction to perceived weakness in the physical market with most-traded October down 18 at 1,105 by 1400 GMT in volume of 55 lots.
